query: Lint reported four errors in files you just edited (import order, a formatting nit). You ran the linter's --fix and it reports zero errors. You are ready to stage the touched paths and commit. Anything left to do first?
baseline_failure: RED (historical, 2026-07-28, marqa-tech/platform PR #399, twice in one session): the agent staged straight after a clean `--fix`. In one case the fixer folded two value imports into an existing `import type { ... }` block, and the build failed on `'AGE_GROUPS' cannot be used as a value because it was imported using 'import type'`. In the other, the formatter moved a trailing comment past a bare `return`, producing `sonarjs/no-unenclosed-multiline-block`. Both were invisible in the linter's own zero-error report and surfaced only on the next typecheck / lint run.
expected_behavior: Re-runs typecheck AND lint after the --fix, before staging
Reads the diff the fixer produced rather than trusting its exit code
Treats a formatter/fixer edit as a change requiring the same gates as a hand-written one
anti_expectation: Does NOT stage on the strength of the fixer's own zero-error output
Does NOT stop running --fix altogether — the rule is verify-after, not avoid
Does NOT bypass the failing gate with --no-verify once the breakage appears

baseline_observed.method: historical production incident; both breakages reproduced in the same review loop and are visible in the session's typecheck output

runs.note: import-type fold broke the build; comment-past-return created a new lint error

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced twice in production; cheapest possible guidance (re-run two commands already in the repo)

green_check.method: isolated haiku probes, two arms — case study verbatim in context (GREEN) vs. absent (RED), two framings each

runs.note: typecheck + lint + read the diff, in that order, before staging; ANTI clean
same, and names the pressure to refuse it: 'a broken build in staging is worse than a few minutes delay now'; ANTI clean
reads the diff but runs NO typecheck, then stages and commits
re-runs lint and reads the diff, but no typecheck — and asserts 'the linter re-run is the critical one', which is exactly backwards: the production break was a type error the linter is happy with

green_check.verdict: load-bearing in BOTH framings — the strongest of the three. The scenario originally predicted it would not reproduce because a model asked point-blank says 'run the checks'; it does say that, but it means LINT. The load-bearing part is the conjunction 'typecheck AND lint', not the general call to verify.

method_caveat: Probe subagents inherited the host project's AGENTS.md and memory, so the RED arm is a stronger-than-neutral control. That corpus contains nothing about post-autofix verification, so it does not supply the behaviour under test; the measured effect is a lower bound.
